[Interview, 2010-04-07, Talk of the Nation]
HOST: And Ken?

HOST: You've published opinions.
GUEST: Yes, abortion rights, and the last thing the Obama administration wants to be doing right now is having a fight about abortion rights.

HOST: So better to have somebody who would be another thing that they're interested in younger than Judge Wood.
GUEST: Absolutely. Elena Kagan is a full 10 years younger than Judge Wood. She doesn't have a track record. What we do know about her is that she went into Harvard Law School as the dean, after having served in the Clinton administration, and was able to get sort of the factions to get along. It's sort of the academic equivalent of brokering the Arab-Israeli peace accords. And so she's got a lot of conservative support.

HOST: And but able to use that magnificent phrase: I could not talk about an issue that may come before me on the court.
GUEST: Exactly. We don't know anything about Elena Kagan's stands on so many issues, and we do but the one thing that we do know is that we're not going to learn anything more during her confirmation hearing.

HOST: Let's get Michael on the line, Michael calling from Cape Cod.

HOST: And a friend of the president's as well.
GUEST: And a friend of the president's, and he's African-American. I have not seen his name mentioned lately. I know he's in a tough re-election fight, and I think sort of going back to what we said, I think the administration's inclination right now is to go and try and get this done as painlessly as possible and to move on to other things. But you know, a lot of people have talked about him as a possible nominee.

HOST: Another governor who's been mentioned, Janet Napolitano last time around.
GUEST: Janet Napolitano was mentioned last time around. You do not hear her name mentioned much this time around. I think I've got three words for you: The system works.

HOST: Right, okay.
GUEST: And the system is working now.

HOST: Go ahead. You're on the air.

HOST: So a Republican...
GUEST: Lots of bipartisan credentials.

HOST: And...
GUEST: And he would be the first Asian-American. I know that State Department legal adviser Harold Koh has also been mentioned as a possibility for the same reason. I apologize...

HOST: Harold Koh, a champion of the liberals too.
GUEST: A champion of the liberals, which is why he will not be nominated. I don't know, unfortunately, much about the California justice.
